LLM03.name: Supply Chain
LLM03.applicability: Applicable -- the system depends on third-party PyPI/npm packages and runtime-downloaded Hugging Face model weights.
huggingface_model_artifacts: sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 (embedding, listed but the frozen runtime uses BM25 sparse retrieval, not embeddings)
cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2 (reranker, downloaded from Hugging Face at runtime, no pinned revision/hash in code)
LLM03.current_control: requirements.txt direct dependencies are exact-pinned; package-lock.json exists and npm audit reports 0 known vulnerabilities in the resolved tree.
LLM03.residual_risk: Known CVEs in transitively-pulled Python packages (see packages_with_known_vulns) are not tracked or gated by any CI step (none exists per the project's own 'Do Not Build: CI/CD pipelines' scope decision); model artifact integrity is not verified.
real_gaps: 38 known CVEs across 5 pinned Python packages
7 frontend devDependencies use ^/~ ranges, not exact pins
no Python lockfile -- requirements.txt pins only direct dependencies; transitive dependency versions (e.g. transformers, pulled in by sentence-transformers) are not pinned or reproducible
Hugging Face model downloads have no pinned revision/hash -- a model re-upload under the same name would be fetched silently on a clean cache

LLM06.name: Excessive Agency

final_runtime.evidence: backend/routes/review.py hardcodes agent_used=False, agent_steps=0 on every response (grep-verified); backend/app.py's module docstring states neither endpoint uses an agent or routing; grep for any import of pipeline.agent or pipeline.agent_v2 under backend/ found none.
final_runtime.no_automatic_legal_approval: confirmed -- every response carries needs_human_review/review_reason fields and the API never auto-approves/rejects; a human is the final decision-maker by construction.

pipeline_agent_py.used_by: T029 selective-agent research path only (scripts/, notebooks/, never backend/)

pipeline_agent_v2_py.used_by: E10/E11 research path only, never backend/

limits.deterministic_fallback: falls back to A2 (non-agent) on any limit

LLM06.current_control: Architectural separation: the live product path (backend/) never imports agent modules at all, not merely 'disabled by a flag' -- there is no code path from an HTTP request to an agent call in this codebase today.
LLM06.residual_risk: If a future change wires pipeline/agent.py or agent_v2.py into the backend, the existing bounded limits (steps/tool-calls/cost/wall-clock) would apply, but there is currently no test that would fail if that wiring were added carelessly (e.g. without re-checking the cost ceiling) -- a regression-guard gap, not a live vulnerability.
